To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HTL is a new language for hard realtime programming; (2) HTL programs are guaranteed to meet timing constraints; (3) HTL is extensible in both dimensions; (4) HTL is implemented on top of an event-driven real-time operating system.

HTL is a programming language for hard real-time systems, that HTL programs are guaranteed to satisfy their timing constraints by the compiler, and that HTL is extensible in two orthogonal dimensions without changing their time behavior.
HTL provides a hierarchical, compositional, and extensible programming language for real-time tasks that is suitable for use in embedded systems.

we have designed and implemented a language that is expressive and flexible enough for a wide range of real-time applications, while at the same time being able to guarantee timing correctness of the resulting programs.

a language that supports timing invariance in a hierarchical way can greatly facilitate the design and implementation of hard real-time systems.
the coordination of real-time tasks can be achieved by specifying timing constraints in a language that is both expressive and amenable to compilation.
